sample_unit: API calls (705 panoramic radiographs x 12 conditions x 3 models)

links.outcome: Change in LLM clinical recommendations when patient race/ethnicity and sex cues varied in prompts
links.effect: All three models altered recommendations with demographic cues; Claude showed significant race effects (p<.001); GPT-5.4 Hispanic invasiveness β=+0.052; Gemini Black invasiveness β=+0.026; all shifts <6% of one category width.
links.quote: All three models altered recommendations when demographic cues were introduced.

links.outcome: Model-specific sensitivity of recommendations to demographic subgroup cues
links.effect: Demographic prompt cues produced small but systematic shifts in recommendations, with model-specific sensitivity profiles; no Race × Sex interactions significant.
links.quote: Demographic prompt cues produced small but systematic shifts in multimodal LLM clinical recommendations for dental radiographs, with model-specific sensitivity profiles.

links.outcome: Inter-model diagnostic agreement under control prompts
links.effect: Cohen's κ = 0.009-0.159, near chance agreement between models.
links.quote: Inter-model agreement was near chance, indicating that model choice currently introduces more variability than any demographic label.

unlisted_practices: Inter-model agreement assessment across commercial multimodal LLMs for dental radiograph interpretation

screen.reason: The study conducts an algorithmic bias and sensitivity audit on multimodal LLMs evaluating dental radiographs under varying demographic prompt cues; it evaluates model behavior/fairness rather than a specific deployment guardrail or practice.
